label: Vinci
summary: Hill town west of Florence from which Leonardo's family took its name; the family household of his grandfather Antonio was there.

claims.statement: Leonardo is listed as a member of his grandfather Antonio's household at Vinci in the Florentine tax return (catasto) of 1457.
Coordinates given in the Itinerario Vinciano: 43.7837 N, 10.925 E.

background.text: Church: Baptism in the church of Santa Croce at Vinci is the accepted tradition C ; the birth record itself names no church, and no patronal dedication for the village is asserted here
Government: Rural commune under the Republic of Florence. The castle of Vinci, formerly a stronghold of the Conti Guidi, passed to Florentine control in the thirteenth century

Terrain and water: Northwestern slopes of the Montalbano massif, terraced in olives and vines above the lower Arno valley. Anchiano, the traditional site of his infancy, lies about two kilometers north of the village
Economy: Agrarian: olive oil, wine, silkworm rearing. The paternal family were notaries, a profession that tied the household to the urban economy of Florence
